A.explanation: Reverses the Doppler shift - approaching source must give higher than $2000\text{ Hz}$ and receding source lower than $2000\text{ Hz}$.

B.explanation: Reverses the two frequencies - $1840\text{ Hz}$ is the receding value and $2190\text{ Hz}$ is the approaching value.

C.explanation: Has the correct high-low order but both values are slightly too small, from rounding or using $v$ incorrectly in the denominator.

D.explanation: Gives increased frequency about $2190\text{ Hz}$ on approach and decreased frequency about $1840\text{ Hz}$ on recession, matching $f_o = f_s v/(v \mp v_s)$.

hints: Notice the given $v_s = 30.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $v = 340\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and source $f_s = 2000\text{ Hz}$ - the observed wavelength is shortened on approach and stretched on recession.
Connect this to the moving-source Doppler equations $f_o = f_s v/(v - v_s)$ towards the man and $f_o = f_s v/(v + v_s)$ away from the man.
Calculate $340/310 \times 2000$ and $340/370 \times 2000$ and check which column must be above $2000\text{ Hz}$ and which must be below.
walkthrough: Identify the situation as Doppler effect with moving source and stationary observer: source speed $v_s = 30.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$, wave speed $v = 340\text{ m s}^{-1}$, source frequency $f_s = 2000\text{ Hz}$.
State the rule: motion towards compresses waves so observed wavelength $\lambda_o = (v - v_s)/f_s$ and $f_o$ increases; motion away stretches waves so $\lambda_o = (v + v_s)/f_s$ and $f_o$ decreases.
For approach, use $f_{towards} = f_s \times v/(v - v_s) = 2000 \times 340/(340 - 30.0)$.
Substitute: $f_{towards} = 2000 \times 340/310 = 2000 \times 1.0968 \approx 2194\text{ Hz}$, which to 3 significant figures matches $2190\text{ Hz}$.
For recession, use $f_{away} = f_s \times v/(v + v_s) = 2000 \times 340/(340 + 30.0)$.

Substitute: $f_{away} = 2000 \times 340/370 = 2000 \times 0.9189 \approx 1838\text{ Hz}$, which to 3 significant figures matches $1840\text{ Hz}$. High frequency towards, low frequency away. This is option D.
